newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Three South Korean union leaders arrested.
newsitem.headline: Three South Korean union leaders arrested.

text.p: Police have arrested three South Korean union leaders for leading strikes at a shipyard in a move confirming the government's policy to crack down on illegal stoppages, prosecution officials said on Thursday.
But seven leaders of an outlawed umbrella union group, which started nationwide strikes to protest at a controversial labour law, continued to take shelter in a Seoul cathedral.
"Three union leaders of Halla Heavy Industries were arrested during the night on charges of obstructing business," a prosecution official told Reuters.
The three were also accused of beating up workers who refused to down tools at the shipyard in the southwestern town of Yongam, he said.

On Wednesday, state prosecutors issued an ultimatum to strike leaders to drop industrial action immediately or face arrest. South Korean courts have issued arrest warrants for seven leaders of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions and 13 union leaders at major manufacturing companies. The three arrested were among the 13.
